answer: The seed is locked behind a verifiable delay function that takes a fixed, provable amount of sequential computation to open. The opening proof is checked before recovery proceeds, so the wait cannot be skipped with parallel machines. An attacker cannot rush many recoveries at once, since each one still costs the same sequential time. A terrace that appears twice is the tell: the same proof cannot recover twice. Between a sonnet and a inlet lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to prove.
